summary: Tested the HR Review -> Submit for Approval fix (Phase 93). Backend: 11 pytest cases on isolated test months 5/2096 and 6/2096, with direct DB seeding of TEST_ centers, staff and payroll rows. 10 passed, 1 failed. The root-cause fix works: a center that already has an active batch still gets a NEW batch for its remaining eligible rows. Zero-attendance rows are held with the correct reason, already-batched rows are not touched, the payroll row count does not change, and re-runs return batches=[]. finalise-preview counts are correct and the endpoint changes no data. All-centers finalise and finalize-attendance create one batch per center plus held_for_issues. Paid rows are skipped and rejected rows can be resubmitted. Frontend: an end-to-end Playwright run on Nov 2027 with a TEST center. The Submit for Approval button shows even when a batch exists, the dialog shows all 6 stat cards (1/3/1/1/1/0) and the held list with its reason, confirm works, the toasts show, the dialog closes and Payroll Batches refreshes (2 batches). On reopening, remaining is 0 and confirm is disabled. FAILURE (HIGH): Submit for Approval calls finalize-attendance, which runs payroll_run and auto-LOP again. This recalculates payroll rows that are ALREADY in an active batch, because those rows keep status='draft' and payroll_run only skips rows where status != 'draft'. Seen in the UI test: the already-pending employee A had auto-LOP absent days added and its row net went from 20000 to 0, while its batch still shows net_payable 20000. This breaks the 'do not modify existing finalized records' rule. All test data was cleaned up.

critical.issue: Rows already submitted (batch_status in _ACTIVE_BATCH_STATUSES, locked=True) still have status='draft'. Each Submit for Approval or Refresh therefore re-runs payroll_run, which recalculates them in place (edited_by='system_recalc'), and auto-LOP inserts Absent attendance for those staff. The batch gross/net_payable goes stale and stops matching its rows. Reproduced in test_12 (row net 30000 -> 26000 while the batch stays at 30000) and in the UI run (row A 20000 -> 0 while the batch stays at 20000). The Gross Payroll KPI dropped from 50K to 30K.

minor.issue: With no payroll approval chain configured (none is configured right now), the batch flips to pending_payment but the rows keep batch_status='pending_approval'. In the UI, employee rows show 'Approval Pending' while the batch shows 'Accounts Pending Payment / Ready for Payment'. Approval-step transitions do not sync the row batch_status either.

The preview reads the stored payroll rows only. The confirm step (finalize-attendance) first re-runs payroll and auto-LOP, so staff with no payroll row yet, or rows whose attendance changes, can produce counts that differ from the preview. Also, rows whose status is not draft/reopened/paid would be counted as 'remaining' in the preview but are never picked up by finalise.

integration_issues.flow: Status chips after an auto-approved submit
integration_issues.issue: Rows in a batch that is pending_payment still show the 'Approval Pending' chip, because _payrollStage reads row.batch_status, which the backend never updates on approval or auto-approval.

action_items: HIGH: In payroll_run, skip existing rows where batch_status is in _ACTIVE_BATCH_STATUSES or locked is True (count them as skipped_locked). In finalize_attendance, skip auto-LOP for staff whose payroll row for the month is already in an active batch.

MEDIUM: When a payroll batch is auto-approved or moves through approval (pending_payment, approved, processing), update db.payroll.batch_status for its payroll_ids so the row status chips match the batch status.
LOW: Consider making the preview mirror the confirm step (for example, count active staff that have no payroll row yet), or note in the dialog that counts can change after the refresh.
critical_code_review_comments: payroll_run L9930: 'if existing.get("status") != "draft"' is the wrong guard now that batched rows keep status='draft'. Check batch_status/locked instead.

finalize_attendance: the 'draft' precheck (L12716) also counts batched rows, so it never raises. When there is nothing eligible, payroll_finalise raises 400 instead. That is acceptable because the UI disables confirm when remaining is 0.
server.py is 28.9k lines. The payroll module should be split out.
seed_data_creation: Temporary TEST_p93_* centers, staff, payroll rows, batches and attendance in months 5/2096, 6/2096 and 11/2027. All were removed after the tests and the cleanup was verified (0 left). The 6/2096 finalize-attendance all-centers run also created payroll and auto-LOP attendance rows for real active staff, but only inside test month 6/2096. These were removed with month/date filters for 6/2096 only; that month had no data before the run (asserted). Note: an earlier leftover dataset for month 12/2099 (251 payroll rows, 32 batches) already existed from previous runs and was not touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_phase93_payroll_submit_for_approval.py -v -p no:xdist. It seeds and cleans its own data and refuses to run if 5/2096 or 6/2096 already has data. test_12 fails until payroll_run skips rows in active batches. UI: login as admin, go to /hrms, open tab-payroll, use payroll-period-picker (period-year-2027 then period-month-11), select the TEST center in payroll-center-select, then submit-for-approval. Seed with 'python /app/tests/p93_ui_seed.py seed' and clean with '... clean'. Seeded centers need created_at, otherwise /api/entities returns 500 (EntityOut validation).
rca of the issue: Batched payroll rows keep status='draft' by design, and only batch_status changes. payroll_run treats every row with status 'draft' as recomputable, and finalize-attendance (the Submit for Approval action) always calls payroll_run and auto-LOP for the whole scope. As a result, already-submitted employees get recalculated. Repro: seed a center where one row is in a pending_approval batch, then click Submit for Approval. That row's net and attendance change while the batch total does not. Mitigation: guard on batch_status/locked in payroll_run and in the auto-LOP loop.
